hook_text: Enslaved people in America sang about Moses and Egypt. But they weren't only singing about the Bible.
clip_script: Go down, Moses, way down in Egypt land, tell old Pharaoh, let my people go. It's a song about the Israelites escaping slavery. Now imagine singing it while picking cotton, under an overseer's whip. Everyone knew who Pharaoh was. Enslaved people in the American South were told they were property. Their marriages didn't count in law. Their children could be sold. But in the quarters at night they built families and communities. They told stories about Brer Rabbit, a small trickster who always outsmarts the bigger animals. They learned to read in secret, though it was against the law. They worked slowly, broke tools, ran away. Every song, every story, every secret lesson said the same thing: we are people, not property.
visual_style: A whiteboard cotton field with a line of singers, musical notes rising; a rabbit outwitting a fox; a candle-lit hand tracing letters; a figure slipping into the trees.
pacing: Gentle song-like opening, building to a strong closing line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and hear the voices of resistance.
